negative_case_interpretation: **Confirmatory classification policy (ANA-01) to be frozen verbatim at S4-01.** D.11 names positive / qualified / inconclusive; plan §6.10 S4-06 adds `negative`. ANA-01 operationalizes: `positive` = all constraints met for both C2−C1 and C2−CR; `negative` = RET-GS upper bound < 0.02, or an ES/LS upper bound below its negative margin (evaluated before `qualified`); `qualified` = point RET-GS ≥ 0.02 with unresolved noninferiority and point ES ≥ −0.02, LS ≥ −0.01; else `inconclusive`; missing pairs → `incomplete` (never imputed). A true zero effect is `negative` for the practical claim.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: S1 uses a 2×10⁶-token held-out set H for P1; D.8 uses a 10⁶-token WikiText-103 validation sample for LM drift.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Two distinct committed sets. H = 2×10⁶ tokens sampled by document from WikiText-103 train (document ids recorded; disjoint from validation by split). Drift = WikiText-103 validation (SD-3).

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: S2 names 300 development edits and ≥1,000 unrelated prompts; D.5 names 200 Q and 200 U.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Q and U are manifest-fixed subsets of the S2 development pool (`manifests/dev/p5_subsets.json`).

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: WikiText-103 validation has roughly 0.28M GPT-2 tokens, not 10⁶.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Drift set = entire validation split, tokenized once, unique tokens only. Shortfall logged (PA-5). Test split not added. Exact count recorded by DATA-00.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: Correction-track slot retirement reads the owner-edit digest; E.2 forbids routers from receiving fact identity.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Router API has no access to slot metadata. Retirement is a `Cap.update(..., revision=RevisionEvent)` path enabled only when the stream item carries a revision record, on the correction track only. A test asserts `RoundContext` carries no digest except as opaque RNG key material.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: F.6 leaves the ePC solver, step size and stopping to S0; the production run used one relaxation step (and a T-schedule 1…64 across the run; see DEC-006).
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Declared nominal procedure: simultaneous gradient descent on all error variables (the sibling's `relax_errors`), `error_lr = 0.1`, exactly 8 iterations, errors zero-initialized per call, γ = 1, energy `½Σ‖e‖² + CE(current target only, summed not averaged)`, fp32, retrieval frozen within a call, no stopping rule. 64 iterations is the reference horizon. Label "finite-iteration error credit" unless D.6's convergence test passes.
`l_m = round(m·12/3) = 4, 8, 12` → block outputs `h[3]`, `h[7]`, `h[11]`, the last before `ln_f`. Verified by test in S0-04.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: GRACE reference has no byte budget.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Documented eviction adaptation (lowest use count, then oldest) bounded by the same byte accounting; disclosed in PC-10 and the report. Unadapted B4 also run once on development as parity reference.
zsRE aliases = `answers` list deduplicated after normalization; CounterFact aliases = `[target_new.str]`. Scoring only.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: PC-2 "match the base reference": bitwise or tolerance?
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Cap-off path is the same wrapper code with zero writes, so exact equality (max |Δlogit| = 0) is expected and asserted. Nonzero → report with the kernel identified; ≤ 1e-6 relative tolerated only with that record. Note under DEC-001: writes are always applied as a `[3, d]` array that is all-zero when the cap is off (adding 0.0 is exact in IEEE fp32), so the identity holds by construction; S0-10 still measures it.
Uniform (1/3 each) labelled `cr_profile_uniform`; S3-05 estimates from development C2 routes; if C2 never routes, uniform and logged.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: Use count with multiple prefixes and rounds.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: Increment at most once per (slot, item digest); bounded per-item set cleared at item end. Inference never increments. Test in CAP-02.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: PDF App. B says "PyTorch handles the cap and the harness; JAX is used through the base wrapper only if the checkpoint requires it." The lead's execution directive (DEC-001) says all GPU code is JAX and PC functionality is built on FabricPC.
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) follow the PDF's framework line; (b) follow the lead's directive.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (b). The PDF's framework sentence is an implementation preference, not a threshold, endpoint or arm; the lead is the authority named in PDF Operating rule 5. The consequence the PDF warns about ("cross-framework gradients must be explicitly implemented and tested") is avoided entirely because there is now exactly one framework. Recorded here so the report's deviation table (App. G §8) carries it.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: The plan's "equal to HF `GPT2LMHeadModel` logits exactly" (S0-04a, S0-09 decode parity) assumes the reference runs in the same process. Under DEC-001 the reference (PyTorch) is not importable.
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) skip the HF comparison; (b) compare against stored reference outputs produced once by a CPU-only PyTorch environment kept outside the project env.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (b) via REF-01 (`assets/reference/gpt2/`). Because fp32 GEMMs differ between XLA-on-Blackwell and PyTorch-CPU, exact bitwise equality against the oracle is not expected; the assertion is max |Δlogit| ≤ 1e-3 absolute and argmax agreement at every position, and the measured maximum is recorded. Cap-off identity (SD-10) remains exact because it compares the wrapper with itself.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: The ePC checkpoint recipe (`hdpc-distill`) is PyTorch. PA-1 authorizes regeneration "with the sibling's reproduction recipe".
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) PA-1 cannot fire under DEC-001; (b) PA-1 fires with a JAX re-implementation of the same recipe (REG-00) that reproduces the sibling's math line by line.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (b), with the same ≤ 10 GPU-h bound and the 100-step pilot (REG-01). The JAX run is a *new* checkpoint (as PA-1 already says); the recipe is additionally a re-implementation, which the checkpoint's provenance record states. The sibling's 50M run took 35.7 h on an A100 (its `summary.json`), so the projection may well exceed 10 h; REG-01 decides.
spec_defect_resolutions.status: committed; bound raised to 120 GPU-h by DEC-014

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: F.3 step 3: "Select the bank with the largest positive score, ties by depth." Depth could mean the shallowest (bank 1, farthest from the output) or the deepest bank.
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) smallest bank index first; (b) largest bank index first.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (a): banks are processed "in increasing depth order" everywhere else in F.3, so the tie goes to the smallest index. Exact ties of float scores are rare; recorded so the choice is not silent.

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: F.1/S2: "radius calibration is shared by arms using the same base and read variant"; E.2: zsRE and CounterFact are separate experiments. Is the radius one number per (base, read) pooled over datasets, or one per (base, read, dataset)?
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) pooled (min over datasets); (b) per dataset, shared across arms.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (b). The two streams are separate experiments with different unrelated-prompt structure (CounterFact's neighbourhood prompts share the relation and are *closer* in key space than paraphrases; zsRE's locality prompts are unrelated NQ questions). Per-dataset radii keep the 1% false-fire risk equal across arms within each experiment, which is the criterion's purpose. Both values are stored (`results/S2/radius_calibration.json`: `per_dataset` and `pooled_radii_min_over_datasets`).

spec_defect_resolutions.issue: F.1: "A zero radius matches only an exactly equal key." Keys are float32 functions of the residual; the same residual computed through differently fused kernels (single-sequence call vs a batched dispatch, `vmap` or `lax.map`) differs by ~1e-5 on unit-scale keys, so bit-exact equality is not a stable property of the computation.
spec_defect_resolutions.readings: (a) bit-exact equality (batched evaluation impossible with exact keys; CounterFact runs exact-key); (b) equality within a float32 tolerance.
spec_defect_resolutions.resolution: (b): `KEY_TOL = 1e-4` added to every radius comparison (`dist ≤ ρ + 1e-4`), i.e. "exactly equal" = equal within the reproducibility tolerance for the same computation on different kernels (Op. rule 9 spirit). Positive radii shift by 1e-4, below the 20-quantile calibration grid's resolution (candidates differ by ≥ 0.03). Applied identically to learning and inference; the batched evaluator's parity with the sequential decoder is tested on both datasets.

lora.rule: DEC-017: highest mean development RET-GS (primary endpoint) over both datasets; ties -> the prescribed 1e-4; ES/LS/drift reported, not optimized
